From 6d192b4f2d644d15d9a9f1d33dab05af936f6540 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jonathan Cavitt <jonathan.cavitt@intel.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 15:29:37 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] drm/xe/xe_pagefault: Disallow writes to read-only VMAs

The page fault handler should reject write/atomic access to read only
VMAs.  Add code to handle this in xe_pagefault_service after the VMA
lookup.

v2:
- Apply max line length (Matthew)

Fixes: fb544b844508 ("drm/xe: Implement xe_pagefault_queue_work")
Signed-off-by: Jonathan Cavitt <jonathan.cavitt@intel.com>
Suggested-by: Matthew Brost <matthew.brost@intel.com>
Cc: Shuicheng Lin <shuicheng.lin@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Matthew Brost <matthew.brost@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Matthew Brost <matthew.brost@intel.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260324152935.72444-7-jonathan.cavitt@intel.com
(cherry picked from commit 714ee6754ac5fa3dc078856a196a6b124cd797a0)
Signed-off-by: Rodrigo Vivi <rodrigo.vivi@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_pagefault.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_pagefault.c
index 6bee53d6ffc3..922a4f3344b1 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_pagefault.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_pagefault.c
@@ -187,6 +187,12 @@ static int xe_pagefault_service(struct xe_pagefault *pf)
 		goto unlock_vm;
 	}
 
+	if (xe_vma_read_only(vma) &&
+	    pf->consumer.access_type != XE_PAGEFAULT_ACCESS_TYPE_READ) {
+		err = -EPERM;
+		goto unlock_vm;
+	}
+
 	atomic = xe_pagefault_access_is_atomic(pf->consumer.access_type);
 
 	if (xe_vma_is_cpu_addr_mirror(vma))
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a bug in the Xen page fault handler (`xe_pagefault_service`) where write or atomic access to read-only VMAs was not rejected. The modifications are isolated to a single file:

- **`drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_pagefault.c`**:  
  Added a check after the VMA lookup. If the VMA is read-only and the access type is not `XE_PAGEFAULT_ACCESS_TYPE_READ`, the handler sets an error (`-EPERM`) and jumps to the `unlock_vm` label, preventing the fault from being serviced.

**Relationships**:  
The change directly addresses the missing permission validation in the page fault handling path. By ensuring that write/atomic accesses to read-only memory regions are rejected with `-EPERM`, it closes a security/correctness gap introduced in commit `fb544b844508`. The logic is integrated seamlessly into the existing error handling flow.
